problem_motivation.content: ASSB development is limited by instability and incompatibility at solid-solid interfaces.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: their development is hindered by instability and incompatibility at solid-solid interfaces

problem_motivation.content: Lithium penetration still occurs in Li-metal ASSBs despite stiff ceramic electrolytes, often starting from small interfacial irregularities.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: In Li-metal ASSBs, lithium penetration occurs despite stiff ceramic electrolytes via grain boundaries, often initiated by minor Li/SE interfacial irregularities.

problem_motivation.content: Interfacial instabilities and Li penetration at Li/SE interfaces in ASSBs remain unresolved and poorly understood
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Despite these advantages, ASSBs face critical challenges related to the electrochemical and mechanical stability of the Li/SE interfaces

problem_motivation.content: Li penetration cannot be fully eliminated in ASSBs
problem_motivation.evidence_span: the Li penetration cannot be fully eliminated

problem_motivation.content: ASSBs remain susceptible to dendrite and void formation during fast cycling
problem_motivation.evidence_span: ASSBs remain vulnerable to dendrite and void formation during high-rate Li plating and stripping

problem_motivation.content: Experiments are limited in resolving dynamics and local fields, leaving mechanisms unclear
problem_motivation.evidence_span: however, they remain limited in capturing dynamic dendrite evolution or quantifying local stress, current density, and potential distributions. Consequently, the underlying mechanisms governing Li penetration and interface degradation are not yet fully understood.

problem_motivation.content: Combined effects of pressure, protruded geometry, and exchange current density remain insufficiently explored
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, the combined effects of stack pressure, protruded interfacial geometry, and exchange current density on deposition stability remain insufficiently explored even in static analyses without interface evolution.

problem_motivation.content: Resolving these gaps is needed for predictive guidance on pressure, roughness, and materials selection
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Addressing these gaps would enable more quantitative and predictive guidance for tuning stack pressure, controlling interfacial roughness, and selecting SE or interlayer materials to mitigate unstable Li deposition and dendrite formation.

problem_motivation.content: Uniformly stable Li deposition remains difficult to achieve
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Although achieving uniformly stable Li deposition remains challenging

problem_motivation.content: Reported exchange current densities are uncertain, motivating systematic assessment of their effect.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, experimentally reported exchange current densities are subject to uncertainties. To systematically assess the influence of this parameter on electrodeposition behavior, we performed additional simulations

problem_motivation.content: Lowering interfacial resistance is important for long-term battery performance.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Reducing interfacial resistance is crucial for long-term battery performance.

problem_motivation.content: Because Li3N conductivity is much lower than the solid electrolyte, its effect on ion transfer during cycling must be understood.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: As shown in Table-I, the conductivity of Li3N layer is much less than the SE, and this could affect the ion transfer during cycling of the battery. To understand the relation of the ionic conductivity between the SE and the protective layer the following relation (Eq. S4) has been derived.

prior_approach.content: Monroe and Newman modeled dendrite suppression using modulus criterion and interfacial stress/overpotential effects
prior_approach.evidence_span: Early modeling studies by Monroe and Newman [18,19] showed that dendrite suppression requires SE shear modulus at least twice that of Li metal, with interfacial stress and surface overpotential governing current distribution.

prior_approach.content: Extended models incorporated geometry, stress, nonlinearity, and microstructure
prior_approach.evidence_span: Extended models incorporating interfacial geometry, stress, material nonlinearity, and microstructural effects revealed strong coupling in current distribution [20-24]

prior_approach.content: Phase-field modeling has been used to capture morphological evolution of Li dendrites
prior_approach.evidence_span: To capture the subsequent morphological evolution of Li dendrites, phase-field modeling (PFM) [26-29] has attracted increasing interests.

prior_approach.content: Fracture-mechanics and continuum models used stress-dependent Butler-Volmer kinetics
prior_approach.evidence_span: Fracture-mechanics and continuum models incorporating stress-dependent Butler-Volmer kinetics show that stress-current coupling governs Li plating and crack evolution

prior_approach.content: Tu et al. used a continuum model with conformal defects to study interfacial morphology evolution
prior_approach.evidence_span: Tu et al. [35] used a continuum model incorporating conformal interfacial surface defects to investigate the evolution of interfacial morphology during cycling of Li deposition.

prior_approach.content: Verma et al. modeled a perfectly conformal interface with sinusoidal roughness
prior_approach.evidence_span: Verma et al. [36] developed a model assuming perfect conformal contact at the Li/SE interface, where interfacial surface roughness was represented by a sinusoidal perturbation.

prior_approach.content: Prior strategies to improve deposition stability include artificial interlayers, external pressure, denser SEs, HSEA pairing, optimized SE composition, anode-free designs with buffer layers, and interface engineering
prior_approach.evidence_span: Key strategies explored to improve deposition stability include the use of artificial interlayers [38-40], application of external pressure to reduce interfacial resistance [38,40-43], increasing SE density (>95%) [44], high-shear-modulus alloy (HSEA) pairing of alloy anodes and electrolytes [45], optimization of SE composition,44 adoption of anode-free architectures with buffer layers between the current collector and SE [47,48], and interface engineering approaches [49-53].

prior_approach.content: The study adopts the stress-modified Butler-Volmer formulation from McMeeking et al.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The Butler-Volmer equation from McMeeking et al. [62] can be written as

prior_approach.content: The treatment of mechanical contribution follows Deshpande and McMeeking (2023).
prior_approach.evidence_span: Accordingly, following Deshpande and McMeeking (2023) [62], we express the mechanical contribution to the overpotential in terms of σ n .

prior_approach.content: The Li3N-Li discs were prepared using a gas-phase reaction procedure reported by Tang et al.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The Li3N-Li discs were obtained by single-step facile gas phase reaction between Li-metal and N2 gas using the procedure mentioned by Tang et al. [54,55].

prior_approach.content: Prior work and general understanding hold that protective coatings suppress dendrites and improve performance by buffering the Li/SE interface.
prior_approach.evidence_span: It is well established that protective coatings play a critical role in suppressing Li dendrite growth and improving overall battery performance by acting as buffer layers that isolate SEs from the Li metal anode [66].

prior_approach.content: Recent work by Yao et al. used a softer Ag-C composite interlayer.
prior_approach.evidence_span: recent work by Yao et al. [68] demonstrated that use of Ag-C composite which is a softer interlayer

prior_limitation.content: Modulus-based prior modeling is insufficient because Li penetration still occurs despite satisfying the criterion due to surface defects
prior_limitation.evidence_span: yet experiments show that Li penetration can still occur despite meeting the modulus criterion, primarily due to surface defect morphology [14-17,25]

prior_limitation.content: Previous studies did not fully examine how protruded morphology versus smooth interfaces affects overpotential and deposition under varied loading and kinetics
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Previous studies did not fully explore how variations in protruded interfacial morphology, compared with a smooth interface, influence overpotential and Li deposition behaviors under mechanical loading, applied current density, and variations of exchange current density.

prior_limitation.content: Real interfacial gaps, voids, microcracks, and grain-boundary transport are excluded from the model.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: do not account for interfacial gaps, void formation, microcracks, or grain-boundary transport.

rejected_alternative.content: The study does not use phase-field modeling because it focuses on static stress and current distributions for fixed geometry
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Although PFM of Li/SE interface evolution is our long-term goal, this study will primarily focus on static stress and current density distributions of given Li/SE geometry. Therefore, we explicitly model the interfacial kinetics through a modified Butler-Volmer equation rather than a phase-field formulation.

rejected_alternative.content: The model deliberately excludes full cycling, time-dependent evolution, distributed defects, dendrite/crack/void/contact-loss processes, and morphology evolution
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Full electrochemical cycling, time-dependent interface evolution, and continuously distributed surface defects are not considered. In addition, the study does not include dendrite initiation, crack propagation, void growth, contact loss, or morphological evolution during cycling.

rejected_alternative.content: The study avoids full cycling, time-dependent evolution, and distributed defects because they add complex interactions beyond scope.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Full electrochemical cycling, time-dependent interface evolution, and continuously distributed surface defects are not considered. Although these features better represent real systems, they introduce complex interactions that are beyond the scope of this study.

inspiration_source.content: The findings motivate engineering artificial interlayers to control interfacial current distribution.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: With these insights, we also discuss the potential of engineering artificial interlayers to modulate interfacial current distributions

inspiration_source.content: The roughness geometry is based on experimental surface roughness data around 100 nm.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: We are guided by experimental SE surface roughness data which is about 100 nm.

causal_claim.content: Large stress variations around elongated surface protrusions cause nonuniform lithium deposition.
causal_claim.evidence_span: We find that prominent stress variations around elongated surface protrusions are the key to nonuniform Li deposition

causal_claim.content: Without stress variations, lithium deposition becomes uniform even on a rough surface.
causal_claim.evidence_span: without which Li deposition becomes uniform even on a rough surface

causal_claim.content: At higher current-density ratios, high interfacial resistance from roughness-induced area becomes dominant.
causal_claim.evidence_span: otherwise the high interfacial resistance due to surface-roughness-induced interfacial area becomes dominant

causal_claim.content: Stress-current coupling governs Li plating and crack evolution
causal_claim.evidence_span: stress-current coupling governs Li plating and crack evolution

causal_claim.content: Surface or material inhomogeneities drive nonuniform deposition
causal_claim.evidence_span: with surface or material inhomogeneities driving nonuniform deposition

causal_claim.content: Lower exchange current density promotes more uniform Li growth
causal_claim.evidence_span: lower exchange current density promoting more uniform Li growth

causal_claim.content: Defects cause localized current concentration and nonuniform current density
causal_claim.evidence_span: Their results showed that current preferentially concentrates near defects, producing a nonuniform normal current density distribution.

causal_claim.content: Increasing external pressure enhances deposition stability at low shear modulus ratio
causal_claim.evidence_span: increasing external pressure enhances deposition stability when the shear modulus ratio is low

causal_claim.content: Increasing applied current density increases deposition instability
causal_claim.evidence_span: deposition instabilities become more pronounced with increasing applied current density

causal_claim.content: Greater interfacial roughness promotes transport-driven instability
causal_claim.evidence_span: greater surface roughness at the metal/electrolyte interface promotes transport-driven instabilities

causal_claim.content: Mechanical stress primarily drives nonuniform Li deposition
causal_claim.evidence_span: mechanical stress is the primary driver of non-uniform Li deposition

causal_claim.content: Roughness geometry governs stress variations and promotes preferential growth at protrusions
causal_claim.evidence_span: The geometry of surface roughness governs local stress variations and promotes preferential Li growth at extruded features.

causal_claim.content: Higher exchange current density and lower interfacial resistance increase the dominance of mechanical stress effects
causal_claim.evidence_span: the influence of mechanical stress becomes increasingly dominant at high exchange current densities and low interfacial resistance

causal_claim.content: Coupling to the mechanical field supplies interfacial normal stress that affects reaction kinetics.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the coupling with the mechanical field provides the interfacial normal stress influencing the reaction kinetics.

causal_claim.content: Normal stress, exchange current density, and applied/interfacial current density all influence overpotential.
causal_claim.evidence_span: indicating that the normal stress, exchange current density, and applied current density ( ~ iBV ) all affect the overpotential.

causal_claim.content: Electrodeposition can be dominated by mechanics at high stack pressure, low interfacial current density, or high exchange current density.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Eq. (15) indicates that the electrodeposition behavior could be dominated by mechanical effects under high stack pressures, low interfacial current densities, or high exchange current densities

causal_claim.content: Sufficient pressure should plastically deform Li and smooth deposition inhomogeneities.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Ideally, this pressure should be sufficient to induce plastic deformation in the Li metal, helping to smooth out inhomogeneities caused by uneven deposition.

causal_claim.content: Differences in roughness area partly cause overpotential differences by changing interfacial current density.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The variation in overpotential among the different roughness geometries partly arises from differences in the total interfacial area... the elongated ellipse increases the interfacial area and consequently reduces the magnitude of the interfacial current density

causal_claim.content: Including mechanical effects increases the overpotential magnitude by about 0.2 mV.
causal_claim.evidence_span: when mechanical effects are included, the magnitude of the overpotential increases by 0.2 mV in all cases

causal_claim.content: A 1% decrease in normal current density changes overpotential by about 0.26 mV.
causal_claim.evidence_span: A 1% decrease in normal current density corresponds to an overpotential change of approximately 0.26 mV

causal_claim.content: Accounting for mechanical effects produces noticeable current redistribution and nonuniform deposition.
causal_claim.evidence_span: when mechanical effects are taken into account, a noticeable change in the normal current distribution is observed. This variation corresponds to non-uniform Li-metal deposition.

causal_claim.content: Neglecting stress keeps Li deposition rate nearly uniform even on rough surfaces.
causal_claim.evidence_span: If mechanical stress is neglected, Li ion deposition rate remains almost uniform even on a rough surface.

causal_claim.content: Current-density variations directly produce comparable local deposition-rate variations by Faraday’s law.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the local deposition rate is proportional to current density via Faraday’s law. Therefore, a relative variation in current density (e.g., ~0.1–0.5%) directly translates to a comparable relative difference in local deposition rate.

causal_claim.content: Persistent local deposition-rate differences can accumulate over cycling into measurable height variations.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Over extended cycling, such persistent differences can accumulate and lead to measurable height variations.

causal_claim.content: As in plating, interfacial area differences partly control stripping overpotential through current density changes.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These differences are partly governed by the total interfacial area associated with each geometry. The flat ellipse produces an area similar to the smooth interface, whereas the elongated ellipse increases the interfacial area and correspondingly lowers the interfacial current density.

causal_claim.content: Including mechanical effects under stripping uniformly decreases overpotential by about 0.6 mV.
causal_claim.evidence_span: When mechanical effects are included, the resulting change in overpotential for the flat interface is ~0.6 mV. As in plating, this leads to a uniform decrease of 0.6 mV across all three cases of surface roughness

causal_claim.content: Very large exchange current density makes kinetic overpotential negligible relative to mechanical stress.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In this regime, the kinetics effect on overpotential becomes negligible relative to the effect of mechanical stress.

causal_claim.content: Minimal stripping of previously deposited Li leads to very rapid growth.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Once deposited, the Li is not stripped significantly, which in turn leads to very rapid growth.

causal_claim.content: Nonuniform deposition and stripping rates enhance dendrite growth.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This nonuniform ion deposition/stripping rate enhances the growth of the dendrite.

causal_claim.content: Lower interfacial resistance makes the stress contribution more significant.
causal_claim.evidence_span: When interfacial resistance decreases, the ratio of  iBV / io  becomes smaller, leading to significant stress contribution.

causal_claim.content: Nonuniform normal stress causes nonuniform ion deposition/stripping, which promotes dendrite growth.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the nonuniform distribution of interfacial normal stress results in nonuniform ion deposition and stripping rates, which are undesirable and contribute to dendrite growth.

causal_claim.content: Effective ionic conductivity is highly sensitive to the thickness ratio of protective layer to solid electrolyte.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the effective ionic conductivity for the SE with the protective layer is highly sensitive to the thickness ratio between the Li₃N protective layer (t) and the argyrodite SE (L).

causal_claim.content: A softer interfacial coating can reduce normal stress variation by better matching lithium's elasticity.
causal_claim.evidence_span: a softer interfacial coating material can be advantageous because its elastic properties more closely match those of lithium metal, thereby reducing the variation in normal stress distribution around surface roughness.

causal_claim.content: The relatively hard Li3N layer causes considerable normal stress variation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the protective layer Li₃N considered in this study is comparatively harder, resulting in considerable normal stress variation

causal_claim.content: Because the mechanics-free model contradicts experiments, mechanical coupling is necessary.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Therefore, including the mechanical contribution in the model and coupling it with electrochemistry are indispensable.

causal_claim.content: Stress dominates only when normalized interfacial current density is sufficiently small.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It becomes dominant only when the ratio of the interfacial current density normalized by the exchange current density is significantly small (0.0389 or less for a compression stress of 3 MPa).

causal_claim.content: Battery aging raises interfacial resistance, lowering exchange current density and weakening stress effects on kinetics.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As interfacial resistance increases with battery aging, the exchange current density decreases, and the stress effects on the interfacial kinetics diminish.

causal_claim.content: Surface roughness geometry controls interfacial normal-stress distribution and thereby local deposition behavior.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The geometry of surface roughness governs the distribution of interfacial normal stress, which in turn strongly influences local deposition behavior.

causal_claim.content: Low interfacial resistance increases exchange current density and makes the stress term important.
causal_claim.evidence_span: When the interfacial resistance is low, the exchange current density increases, and the stress term becomes important.

causal_claim.content: Nonuniform stress around roughness causes nonuniform deposition/stripping and leads to dendrite growth.
causal_claim.evidence_span: However, in this case, nonuniform stress distribution leads to nonuniform ion deposition/stripping rates around the surface roughness, resulting in dendrite growth.

causal_claim.content: The Li3N-Li interface enables more efficient charge-transfer kinetics than Li alone.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This result indicates that the electrochemically stable Li–Li₃N/SE interface facilitates more efficient charge-transfer kinetics during lithium plating and stripping.

causal_claim.content: In the low-exchange-current regime, mechanical stress has negligible effect on interfacial kinetics.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Regardless of the roughness geometry, the effect of mechanical stress on interfacial kinetics remains negligible in this regime.

causal_claim.content: At very high exchange current density, including mechanical stress increases the magnitude of overpotential by about 0.4 mV.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In contrast, when the exchange current density is increased to i₀ = 9500 μA/cm² (100× the experimental value), the inclusion of mechanical stress leads to a measurable overpotential change of approximately 0.4 mV using the parameters listed in Table I.

mechanism_principle.content: Surface roughness increases interfacial area, which raises interfacial resistance.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the high interfacial resistance due to surface-roughness-induced interfacial area becomes dominant

mechanism_principle.content: Instability increases because resulting stress cannot redirect Li flux away from protrusions
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: as the resulting stress is insufficient to redirect Li flux away from growing Li protrusions

mechanism_principle.content: Interfacial defects and microstructure can create current localization and preferred Li-penetration pathways.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In practical systems, such features can introduce additional current localization mechanisms (e.g., contact loss) and may provide preferred pathways for Li penetration.

mechanism_principle.content: The model captures mutual electrochemical-mechanical influence through bidirectional coupling at the interface.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This bidirectional coupling captures the mutual influence of electrochemical and mechanical effects at the interface.

mechanism_principle.content: Linear elasticity is reasonable because commonly used solid electrolytes have high modulus and low fracture toughness.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: SE materials commonly used in solid-state batteries tend to have high elastic moduli and low fracture toughness [35] making the assumption of linear elasticity reasonable.

mechanism_principle.content: For interfacial reactions, normal traction is used because lithium insertion occurs normal to the interface.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: for interfacial reactions, lithium insertion occurs normal to the interface, and the relevant quantity is the normal traction.

mechanism_principle.content: Using normal stress is a reasonable approximation in 2D because stress variations are dominated by the normal component.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In the present 2D setting, stress variations are dominated by the normal component, making this a reasonable approximation.

mechanism_principle.content: Hydrostatic compressive stress can exceed yield without more plasticity because yielding depends on deviatoric stress.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Although this value exceeds the yield strength of Li, yielding is governed by the deviatoric stress state, as described by the von Mises yield criterion.

mechanism_principle.content: Mechanical constraint from the solid electrolyte restricts plastic flow and allows elevated compressive stresses to persist.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the lithium metal is mechanically constrained by the surrounding solid electrolyte, which restricts plastic flow and permits elevated compressive stresses to persist under equilibrium conditions.

mechanism_principle.content: Plastic deformation does not fully homogenize interfacial stress because of rough geometry and boundary constraints.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: it does not completely homogenize the interfacial stress distribution because of the geometric roughness and mechanical boundary constraints.

mechanism_principle.content: The linearized Butler-Volmer form makes the separate kinetic and stress contributions explicit.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In the linearized equation (15), interfacial kinetics term ( Rint iBV ) , and mechanical stress term ... are expressed as a simple addition. This straightforward expression highlights the relative significance of mechanical stress in a simplified form.

mechanism_principle.content: The reason for this behavior is variation in interfacial normal stress around roughness.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The key reason for this is attributed to the interfacial normal stress variation around the surface roughness.

hypothesis_statement.content: Mechanical stress plays a critical role in determining interfacial current distribution in roughened argyrodite electrolytes.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Our theoretical analysis and simulation studies highlight the critical role of mechanical stress in interfacial current distribution.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study proposes clarifying the influence of mechanical stress by selectively including or excluding stress contributions in simulations
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: the mechanical stress contribution can be selectively included and excluded in the simulations, allowing its influence on interfacial kinetics to be clarified directly

hypothesis_statement.content: This work investigates how mechanical stress and interfacial roughness affect metal electrodeposition in ASSBs
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This study aims to computationally investigate the effects of mechanical stress and interfacial surface roughness geometry on metal electrodeposition in metal/inorganic-SE systems employed in ASSBs.

hypothesis_statement.content: Stable Li deposition should be achieved using low-resistance interlayers with high ionic conductivity and low elastic modulus
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: These findings indicate that achieving stable Li deposition requires the use of low-resistance interlayers with high ionic conductivity and low elastic modulus.

hypothesis_statement.content: Careful tuning of electrochemical and mechanical parameters can improve interface stability and suppress dendrites
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: our study demonstrates that careful tuning of electrochemical and mechanical parameters can enhance interface stability and suppress dendritic growth.

hypothesis_statement.content: Using isolated roughness features should allow controlled study of how geometry affects stress, current density, and overpotential.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Instead, isolated surface roughness features are assumed, enabling a controlled investigation of how roughness geometry influences interfacial stress, current density distribution, and overpotential.

hypothesis_statement.content: Because deposition is enhanced and stripping is reduced around the elongated ellipse, its growth is expected.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Combined with the prior analysis of high Li deposition rate around the elongated ellipse, growth of elongated ellipse is anticipated.

hypothesis_statement.content: A protective layer could address the trade-off by acting as a buffer zone.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To address this trade-off, a protective layer can be used as a buffer zone.

hypothesis_statement.content: Softer interfacial materials may enable more uniform plating/stripping and suppress dendrites even at low interfacial resistance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Softer interfacial materials may promote a more uniform ion plating/stripping rate and suppress dendrite growth, even when the interfacial resistance remains relatively low.

hypothesis_statement.content: A soft buffer layer may reduce stress nonuniformity while preserving low interfacial resistance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To mitigate this issue, a soft buffer layer may be used to reduce the nonuniformity of normal interfacial stress distribution while maintaining reduced interfacial resistance.

evidence_result.content: Theory and simulations indicate that mechanical stress critically affects interfacial current distribution.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our theoretical analysis and simulation studies highlight the critical role of mechanical stress in interfacial current distribution.

evidence_result.content: Parametric study shows stress effects dominate overpotential and current distribution at low interfacial-to-exchange current density ratios.
evidence_result.evidence_span: our parametric study elucidates that stress effects dominate the overpotential and current distribution under low interfacial current density to exchange current density ratios

evidence_result.content: Tu et al. found current concentrates near defects and normal current density becomes nonuniform
evidence_result.evidence_span: Their results showed that current preferentially concentrates near defects, producing a nonuniform normal current density distribution.

evidence_result.content: Verma et al. found higher external pressure improves stability when modulus ratio is low
evidence_result.evidence_span: Their results showed that increasing external pressure enhances deposition stability when the shear modulus ratio is low.

evidence_result.content: Higher applied current density worsens deposition instability because stress cannot redirect Li flux
evidence_result.evidence_span: deposition instabilities become more pronounced with increasing applied current density, as the resulting stress is insufficient to redirect Li flux away from growing Li protrusions.

evidence_result.content: Greater surface roughness promotes transport-driven instabilities
evidence_result.evidence_span: Furthermore, greater surface roughness at the metal/electrolyte interface promotes transport-driven instabilities.

evidence_result.content: The study finds mechanical stress is the main driver of nonuniform Li deposition even with roughness present
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our results reveal that mechanical stress is the primary driver of non-uniform Li deposition, even in the presence of surface roughness.

evidence_result.content: Surface roughness geometry controls local stress variations and preferential Li growth at extrusions
evidence_result.evidence_span: The geometry of surface roughness governs local stress variations and promotes preferential Li growth at extruded features.

evidence_result.content: Mechanical stress becomes more dominant at high exchange current density and low interfacial resistance
evidence_result.evidence_span: the influence of mechanical stress becomes increasingly dominant at high exchange current densities and low interfacial resistance.

evidence_result.content: Rough surfaces formed during manufacturing or polishing can contribute to dendrite growth.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In reality, minute rough surfaces are formed during the smoothing process or after fine surface polishing of the SE in cell manufacturing, which can gradually contribute to potential dendrite growth.

evidence_result.content: Applying compressive stack pressure is essential to maintain intimate interfacial contact during operation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Applying compressive stack pressure is essential during cell operation to maintain intimate contact at the interface.

evidence_result.content: Different roughness geometries produce different normal stress distributions, with elongated ellipses showing the largest stress drop.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The rough surfaces exhibited distinct normal stress distributions depending on the geometry... the elongated ellipse has shown the greatest variation, with the compressive stress dropping from 3 MPa to approximately 1.6 MPa.

evidence_result.content: Introducing elongated roughness raises the plating overpotential more than flat or circular roughness.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For an elongated elliptical roughness, the overpotential rises further to -25.516 mV... The circular roughness produces an overpotential that lies between these two cases

evidence_result.content: The elongated ellipse differs from the flat ellipse by about 0.4 mV in overpotential.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the numerical results indicate that the elongated ellipse produces an overpotential that differs from the flat ellipse by about 0.4 mV.

evidence_result.content: The simulations indicate mechanical stress is the main cause of nonuniform lithium deposition.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The simulations suggest that mechanical stress is the primary contributor to deposition non-uniformity

evidence_result.content: Without mechanical effects, normal current density changes very little and deposition is nearly uniform.
evidence_result.evidence_span: When mechanical effects are not considered, there is minimal change in the normal current density indicating almost uniform Li-metal deposition.

evidence_result.content: The elongated ellipse shows greater current concentration and a larger stressed-vs-unstressed difference than flatter shapes.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the magnitude of normal current density at the center of the elongated elliptical roughness (~98.75 μA/cm²) exceeds that in the region away from the roughness (~98.32 μA/cm²)... For this geometry, the difference between the stressed and unstressed cases increases to approximately 0.5 %.

evidence_result.content: Elongated elliptical roughness causes the most pronounced current-density variation and tends to enhance deposition around the extrusion.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the elongated elliptical shape, the variation in current density is more pronounced... These results show that the elongated elliptical shape tends to enhance Li deposition around the extrusion

evidence_result.content: Under stripping, flat and elongated roughness slightly reduce overpotential relative to a smooth interface.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Introducing a flat elliptical roughness reduces the overpotential slightly to 25.881 mV, while an elongated elliptical roughness further reduces it to 25.516 mV.

evidence_result.content: During stripping, stress lowers current density along the elongated protrusion relative to the unstressed case.
evidence_result.evidence_span: A lower magnitude of normal current density is observed along the contour of the elongated protrusion (~97.17 μA/cm²) compared to the case without mechanical stress (~98.33 μA/cm²), indicating slower Li stripping in the stressed condition.

evidence_result.content: At very low exchange current density, stress effects on overpotential are negligible.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure S4(a) indicates that the effect of stress remains negligible in this regime.

evidence_result.content: At low exchange current density, stressed and unstressed current distributions are nearly identical, so stress hardly affects deposition.
evidence_result.evidence_span: At very low exchange current densities... the spatial distribution of normal current density with and without mechanical stress remains nearly identical... indicating that mechanical stress has a negligible effect on the Li deposition rate.

evidence_result.content: At very high exchange current density, stress strongly increases current density near elongated roughness during deposition.
evidence_result.evidence_span: at very high exchange current densities (100× the experimental value), the magnitude of the normal current density near the elongated elliptical interface increases markedly from ~98.2 μA/cm² (without stress) to ~167.7 μA/cm² (with stress)

evidence_result.content: Increasing applied current density 100-fold makes stress influence negligible compared with kinetic effects.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The resulting overpotential distributions for various roughness geometries, with and without mechanical effects, nearly overlap, indicating that the influence of stress remains negligible

evidence_result.content: Under stripping, low exchange current density also makes stress contribution negligible.
evidence_result.evidence_span: When the exchange current density is very small (0.01× the experimental value)... the contribution of mechanical stress to the overpotential becomes negligible

evidence_result.content: At very high exchange current density in stripping, stress strongly lowers current density near elongated roughness.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The magnitude of the normal current density near the elongated elliptical interface decreases markedly from ~97.88 μA/cm² (without stress) to ~27.51 μA/cm² (with stress)

evidence_result.content: With 100-fold higher applied current in stripping, stress has no significant influence compared with kinetics.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The resulting overpotential distributions for different surface roughness geometries, with and without mechanical effects, show no significant influence of stress compared with kinetic effects

evidence_result.content: When exchange current density becomes very large, the stress term becomes important and overpotential stays small enough for linearization.
evidence_result.evidence_span: when the exchange current density becomes extremely large, the stress term gains significance, and the magnitudes of (mechanics-free) overpotential becomes small. In such cases, the use of the linearized form becomes feasible.

evidence_result.content: Large exchange current density causes large current-density variation around rough surfaces, with faster deposition and slower stripping at elongated roughness.
evidence_result.evidence_span: when the exchange current density becomes large, then the normal current density variation around the rough surface becomes large. The high ion deposition rate and low ion stripping rate are observed around the elongated elliptical roughness interface.

evidence_result.content: At high current density, stress effects can generally be ignored unless exchange current density is greatly improved.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Battery operation under high current density is important. As shown in Section 3.3 and Figure S5 and S8, the stress effect can be ignored in this case. However, if there is a significant improvement in increasing the exchange current density, the stress effect can become important.

evidence_result.content: A Li3N protective layer reduces local compressive stress around elongated roughness during plating.

evidence_result.content: With Li3N, plating current density increases while stripping current density decreases around the rough interface.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the magnitude of the normal current density during lithium plating increases approximately to 99.44 μA/cm² from 98.75 μA/cm² in the presence of the Li₃N layer... while stripping, the normal current density magnitude decreases to approximately 95.93 μA/cm² from 97.17 μA/cm²

evidence_result.content: Preliminary experiments with thick SE and thin Li3N showed good cycling, but simulations with a much thinner SE predicted strongly reduced effective ionic conductivity.
